records.name: We Love to Give
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives out groceries, meals, clothing, and hygiene items to neighbors facing hunger or housing trouble, and keeps a community fridge stocked.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at a grocery giveaway, a Love Park serving, or a community fridge refill, or help with the Game Day visits to senior neighbors that run all year. Donations of food and goods are also welcome. People in need can come to the giveaways and servings.

schedule.text: Grocery giveaway at Beloved St. John on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, 12 to 1 pm. Love Park servings on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays, noon to 1 pm or until the food runs out, weather permitting. Community fridge refilled on the 15th of each month.

cost.text: The giveaways and servings are free.

first_step.how: Fill out the Donate and Volunteer form on the website (name, phone, email, then choose Volunteer My Time), or email give@welovetogive.org, before you come to help.
first_step.basis: The giveaways and Love Park servings are open to the public and first come, first served, and the site gives a form, an email and a phone line to start. It does not describe a special welcome for new volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Come to a Saturday giveaway or Love Park serving, or ask to help on a shift. Volunteers help with things like serving meals and organizing donations, and even occasional help counts. The site gives no street address for Beloved St. John or Love Park, and the giveaways and servings are free.
first_visit_tips: Call (267) 433-2227 or email give@welovetogive.org for the address and check-in time, since the site lists no street address for either place.
At Love Park, look for the group's tent.
Servings are weather permitting and first come, first served, so arrive early.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The site gives no street address for Beloved St. John or Love Park and no hours for the Game Day visits, so none are recorded. The Google calendar the site links has no feed address on the pages read, so no calendar_feed. The P.O. box on the contact page is a mailing address, not a drop-off site, and the site lists no donation drop-off hours, so neither is recorded. The community fridges named on the site are in leads_only. The October 2026 podcast item gives the last sign of life.

records.name: We Walk PHL
records.summary: A free walking group that meets in public parks across Philadelphia. Trained local leaders guide about an hour of walking, one to three times a week depending on the park. The program is supported by Parks and Recreation, the Fairmount Park Conservancy and the Department of Public Health.
records.what_you_do: Walk with neighbors for about an hour in a park near you, and get to know people who walk the same route.

schedule.text: Walks last about an hour, one to three a week depending on the park. The fall season runs September 1 to October 31. The Bartram's Garden walk meets Thursdays from 5 to 6 pm at its Welcome Center during its listed seasons.

locations.label: Public parks across Philadelphia (varies by walk)

first_step.how: Register for a walk near you through the program's sign-up link, or call 215-309-5523. Registration is recommended for the Bartram's Garden walk, which meets Thursdays at 5 pm at the Welcome Center.
first_step.basis: Free, open to people of all ages and abilities, led by trained local leaders, with a phone line and a sign-up link. The pages do not say whether first-time walkers get extra help or whether registration is required before the first walk.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each walk lasts about an hour and a trained local leader guides it through a park near you. Walk leaders greet and guide participants, and the pages do not give the pace or distance, so ask the program before you go. The walks are free, and registration is recommended for the Bartram's Garden walk.
first_visit_tips: Go to the Bartram's Garden Welcome Center at 5400 Lindbergh Boulevard for the Thursday walk, and look for the walk leaders at the start.
Ask the program about pace and distance if you want an easier walk.
Check the park and time before each walk, since the schedule varies by park.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The GivePulse sign-up page returned HTTP 403, so the sign-up route here comes from the city page and the walk listings, and the portal itself was not read. The Bartram's Garden event page sits in a 2026 series that ran May 7 to June 25, with a walk dated June 18, which gives last_sign_of_life 2026-06. The earlier 2026-09 date came from a listing that prints no year, so it was replaced. The Bartram's Thursday walk is a listed season, not a year-round weekly walk, so the schedule text was narrowed. A Thursday September 17 to October 29 listing prints no year, so it is not used as dated evidence. The city post is dated September 10, 2025.

records.name: We3 Gardens
records.summary: A neighborhood garden project that creates shared spaces for growing, learning and gathering in the city. It started with raised beds, flowers, herbs and places to sit.
records.what_you_do: Sit in the Poetry Parklet, see and touch the plants, and take part in planting days when they are announced. You can share ideas through the project's survey, or support the project with donations, materials or a partnership.

schedule.text: The project holds planting days, but the page lists no dates. Sign up for updates on the project page to hear when they are.

locations.label: Poetry Parklet, West Philadelphia (no street address published)

first_step.how: Email the project contact on its We3 Gardens page to ask about visiting the Poetry Parklet or joining a planting day.
first_step.basis: The project is public and invites visitors, planting days and support, with a sign-up for updates and an email contact. But the page gives no street address, no hours and no dated planting days, so a first visit is hard to plan.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Poetry Parklet is a small public space in West Philadelphia with plants and places to sit, pause and gather. The page does not give hours, so email before you go. Planting days are the hands-on way to take part, but no dates are listed on the page.
first_visit_tips: Email before you go, since no hours or street address are posted.
Sign up for updates on the project page so you hear about planting days.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The project pages give no street address, hours, or dated planting days, so the location is only West Philadelphia and no last_sign_of_life is set. The What We Do page does not describe the project. The site's support link opens an email. CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia is the fiscal sponsor and Feet First Philly is a grant source, both named on the page and not recorded as groups. The one web search turned up a neighbor survey for a parklet near the Haverford Free Library, but no result named We3 Gardens, so that location was not used.

records.name: The Welcoming Center for New Pennsylvanians
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps immigrants build jobs, businesses, and English and digital skills. Its programs include English and digital skills classes, work readiness tracks, business courses and the Immigrant Leadership Institute, and it offers translation and interpretation help.
records.what_you_do: Join an English or digital skills class, a work readiness track, a business planning course, or the Immigrant Leadership Institute. Translation and interpretation help is available. Volunteers can help with mock interviews, resume help and career guidance.

schedule.text: General English classes meet 9:30 am to 12 pm, two days a week, and start on set dates. Level 1 meets in person in Center City, and higher levels mix in-person and Zoom. Spots are waitlist only.

cost.text: The English, computer, entrepreneurship and work readiness classes are listed as free. The site does not say what the business planning courses cost.

access.notes: Translation and interpretation help is offered. Call 215-557-2626 and staff will connect you with help in your language.

first_step.how: Fill out the waitlist or interest form on the English and digital skills page for the class you want, or call 215-557-2626 to ask which level fits you.
first_step.basis: The classes are free and aimed at immigrants, but most are waitlist only, and some need intermediate English first. Enrolling means a form or a call, so walk-ins are not the way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are free and start on set dates. For General English, Level 1 meets in person in Center City twice a week from 9:30 am to 12 pm, and higher levels mix in-person and Zoom. Joining the waitlist does not guarantee a spot, so ask the office when the next start is.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-557-2626 first, since the site does not list office hours or walk-in rules.
If English is not your first language, ask for help in your language when you call.
The office is on the 4th floor of 211 N 13th St. The site does not say whether there is an elevator, so ask when you call.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The site lists classes as waitlist or interest forms and gives no office hours, so walk-ins are not established. The address shows ZIP 19106 on one page and 19107 on another; this record keeps 19107 as in the tier 1 file. The only dated items are 2027 class start dates and a 2025 annual report with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is set. Volunteering: mock interviews, resume help and career guidance. The volunteer and media contacts are staff email addresses and are not recorded.

records.name: West Philadelphia Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker worship group in West Philadelphia that meets for silent worship on the first and third Sundays of the month, in person or on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Join silent worship on the first and third Sundays at Calvary Center or on Zoom. The site lists no children's program, no childcare, and no committees or volunteer work open to visitors.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am on the first and third Sundays of each month, in person and on Zoom.

locations.label: Calvary Center, upstairs Samaritan Room, enter from 48th Street

cost.text: No cost is listed on the site.

access.notes: The Philadelphia Yearly Meeting listing says the meeting is not wheelchair accessible. The worship room is upstairs, and the site does not mention an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to worship on the first or third Sunday at 10:30 am, entering from 48th Street and going upstairs to the Samaritan Room, or join from home using the Zoom link posted on the website.
first_step.basis: Worship is open to the public at a set time, with a room and a Zoom option, but the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers and the yearly meeting listing has no first-visitor notes.
first_step.what_to_expect: Worship lasts one hour, from 10:30 to 11:30 am, and it is silent, so you can sit and listen. The site does not say whether visitors are expected to speak, or whether anyone greets people at the door. No cost is listed.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes early so you have time for the stairs to the Samaritan Room.
If stairs are a problem, join by Zoom, since the listing says the meeting room is not wheelchair accessible.
Call 267-405-2302 or email wpfmclerk@gmail.com to ask about access before you go.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The meeting's own site has no visitor, newcomer or FAQ page we could reach (its about page returned 404), so first-visit detail comes from the schedule and the Philadelphia Yearly Meeting listing. That listing says the meeting is not wheelchair accessible and has no First Day School or childcare. The site's schedule covers 2026 to 2027 with no month printed, so the earlier last_sign_of_life 2026 (no month) was cleared rather than guessed. Status stays active from tier 1 on the basis of the current schedule and the posted Zoom link.

records.name: West Philly Insight
records.summary: A free weekly meditation group in West Philadelphia that meets at Calvary Community Center on Baltimore Avenue. Most sits are open to anyone, and the Thursday evening sits are listed for BIPOC.
records.what_you_do: Sit with the group in the Insight style, and join the Saturday guided meditation and talk or a weekday sit.

schedule.text: Saturdays 1 to 2 pm: guided meditation, a talk, questions, then tea, open to all. Wednesdays: two half hour sits, 7 to 7:30 am and 7:35 to 8:05 am, open to all. Thursdays: two half hour sits, 7 to 7:30 pm and 7:35 to 8:05 pm, listed for BIPOC.

cost.text: Classes are offered freely. No donation policy is stated.

access.notes: The meeting room is up a flight of stairs from the Baltimore Avenue door. The page does not mention an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to the Saturday 1 to 2 pm session at Calvary Community Center, 4740 Baltimore Ave, or email the group to ask about the weekday sits.
first_step.basis: The Saturday and Wednesday sits are open to all at set times, and the page invites questions by email. Weekly sessions ask only that you contact the group to join the email list. The page does not say whether beginners are welcome or whether instruction is given.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Saturday session runs about an hour: a guided meditation, a talk, questions, then tea. The weekday sits are two 30 minute sits, and you can come to one or both. The sessions are free, and the page does not list a fee or donation.
first_visit_tips: Use the red double doors on Baltimore Avenue, and look for the chalkboard sign out front.
Climb the stairs on your left after the door, and the room is at the top.
Cushions, blankets and yoga mats are kept in a glass cabinet in the room, and you are welcome to use them.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The Thursday evening sits are labelled 'For BIPOC' on the schedule page. The other sessions are open to all, so open_to stays public, and no community id is written because BIPOC is not in the vocabulary. The Fall 2026 retreat on October 10, 2026 is a one-time event and gives the last sign of life; it is not in the schedule text. The page does not say whether beginners are welcome, so the newcomer rating rests on open sits at set times. The Thursday evening start date of September 24 is printed without a year, so it is not recorded.

records.name: West Philly Runners
records.summary: A West Philadelphia running club with a weekly group run in 2, 4 or 6 mile options and a Monday speed workout. It welcomes runners of many paces.
records.what_you_do: Join the Wednesday night group run at your pace, or the Monday speed workout if you want to train harder.

schedule.text: Wednesday night group run from Clark Park, with a 2, 4 or 6 mile choice. Monday speed workout at 6:30 pm in Penn Park. Friday coffee run at 6:30 am from Clark Park.

first_step.how: Go to Clark Park at 44th and Baltimore Avenue for the Wednesday night group run, pick a 2, 4 or 6 mile loop, or subscribe for weekly run news on the club's site.
first_step.basis: The club calls itself welcoming and inclusive, says it is open to beginners and experienced runners alike, and names where the Wednesday run starts and how to get weekly news. It does not say whether you must sign up before a run.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Wednesday run starts at Clark Park and ends at a local bar, and you pick a 2, 4 or 6 mile route. All paces are welcome, though most runners keep at least a 12-minute pace. The site gives no start time for the regular run.
first_visit_tips: Clark Park, at 44th and Baltimore Avenue, is where the Wednesday run starts.
Pick your distance before you start: 2, 4 or 6 miles.
If you want more speed work, the Monday speed workout is at 6:30 pm in Penn Park.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass 2026-10-08. The club's October 14, 2026 event page lists a 1:30 pm start, which does not match the usual Wednesday night slot, so no start time is recorded for the regular run. Cost and sign-up are not stated on the pages read. The club's Facebook group and Instagram are linked from the site but were not read.

notes: Batch of 7 groups, all verdict publish. Searches used: 1 of 1 (cap reached). WebFetch calls: 23, of which 2 failed (GivePulse 403, which is listed under blocked; the We Walk PHL about page on westphillyquakers.org returned 404, which is not a block). No rate limiting seen. Corrections to tier 1: We Walk PHL last_sign_of_life moved from 2026-09 to 2026-06, because the listings for September and May have no year printed; the Bartram's walk is a listed season, not a year-round weekly walk. West Philadelphia Friends Meeting had last_sign_of_life '2026' with no month; cleared to null. West Philly Insight's Thursday evening sits are limited to BIPOC and the summary now says so. West Philly Runners' newcomer rating raised to 4 because the about page says beginners are welcome and says how to start. Leads not recorded as leads_only: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation and the Philadelphia Department of Public Health (city agencies, not groups); CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia (fiscal sponsor of We3 Gardens); Bartram's Garden and Schuylkill River Development Corporation (hosts of the We Walk walks); Calvary Center, Clark Park, Penn Park, Love Park and Haverford Free Library (venues); Philadelphia Yearly Meeting (regional Quaker body); the Welcoming Center's own programs (Global Skills Union Pathways Project, International Professionals Program, MOCA, Immigrant Marche, Breaking Bread, Breaking Barriers), which belong to one organization. The We3 Gardens web search returned a neighbor survey about a parklet near the Haverford Free Library, but no result named We3 Gardens, so that location was not used. The leads_only entries were named on pages whose links did not point to their own sites, so I did not guess URLs for them; they are future research.
